elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 expressly limits audits to “no more than once per 12 months.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 30 days' prior written notice of an audit.
Each audit must be conducted during business hours.
elements.evidence: The added final sentence expressly requires each audit to be conducted “during business hours.”

elements.element: Each audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The added final sentence requires each audit to be conducted “by an independent auditor.”

elements.element: The independent auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The added final sentence requires the independent auditor to be “bound by confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 states that “Vendor bears audit costs” subject to the specified underpayment exception.

elements.element: Customer may be required to pay reasonable audit costs only if the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding 5% for the audited period.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 shifts reasonable audit costs to Customer only where underpayment exceeds five percent for the audited period.

elements.element: Vendor and its auditor may not directly access Customer systems.
elements.evidence: Sections 22.1 and 22.2 prohibit remote or direct access to Customer systems.

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The rolling limitation of no more than once per 12 months is at least as protective as an annual limit.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 15 days' prior notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires 30 days' written notice, which exceeds the fallback notice period.

elements.element: Vendor bears the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 states that Vendor bears audit costs subject to an underpayment exception.

elements.element: Customer may be required to bear audit costs only if underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 shifts reasonable audit costs when underpayment exceeds 5%, including cases where underpayment is more than 5% but does not exceed 10%.

result.reason: The operative language fully achieves the preferred position, notwithstanding the non-operative margin comment. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because its cost-shifting threshold remains 5% rather than 10%. The redline is not minimal because it additionally requires audits to be conducted “off-site where possible,” which is not needed for either stated position. The drafting otherwise preserves the existing shortfall-payment obligation and access exclusions, although the overlapping prohibitions on remote and direct access are somewhat redundant.
